title: WHIP start race tests never check that the rejected request leaves the winner's claim or pending slot intact
test: tests/whipRoutes.test.js: "WHIP starts turned away with 409 while another is allocating leave that start's claim on the room in place" and "public WHIP starts turned away with 409 or 503 leave the running start's claim and the pending-start slot in place" (new tests with their own helper responseOrStuck, placed after the SSRC public-slot test; the two original race tests are untouched)
proof: The gap was missing assertions, not a production defect: lib/whipRoutes.js claims the room (room.whipStarting, room.whipGeneration) and takes a pending-start slot (ownsPublicReservation) only after the 409/503 checks, and releases only what the request owns, so the new tests pass on the current code (node --test tests/whipRoutes.test.js 43 of 43) and no todo case was needed. The two new tests gate createWebRtcTransport on promises, hold a first start inside the transport, and then, before releasing it, send further starts through a helper that returns the response or a 'still allocating' stand-in after 1 s (so a regression fails an assertion instead of hanging): same room, two more requests expect 409 and after each room.whipStarting is still true, room.whipGeneration is unchanged and the transport was entered once; public endpoint with PUBLIC_WHIP_MAX_PENDING_STARTS = 1, each request from its own IP (.1 to .7, so the per-IP limit of 10 is never reached): a 503 from another room, a 409 on the starting room, and a further 503 from another IP, with firstRoom.whipStarting true, its generation unchanged and enteredCount 1 after each. After the winner fails with 500 the room is free and the next start is admitted; after the second start completes, two overlapping starts on fresh IPs admit exactly one (the second is 503, enteredCount stays at 3), which shows the counter is neither positive nor negative. Mutation proof, each mutant applied to lib/whipRoutes.js and reverted with git checkout (the file is unchanged): (1) the 409 branch sets room.whipStarting = false, (2) a shared finally clears whipStarting of the requested room for a request that never claimed it, (3) releasePublicReservation without the ownsPublicReservation guard (a turned-away request gives back a slot it never took, counter still clamped at 0), (4) the same without the Math.max clamp (counter goes negative), (5) releasePublicReservation subtracting 2 (counter ends negative after the winner). The two original race tests ('parallel WHIP starts admit one owner and clear the synchronous claim after failure' and 'public WHIP enforces per-IP and global pending-start limits before media allocation') still PASS on every one of the five mutants; the new tests fail on all five: mutants 1 and 2 at the 'the running start still holds its claim' assertion (true expected, false actual) in both new tests; mutants 3 and 4 at the further 503 from another IP (503 expected, 'admitted and still allocating' actual) in the public test; mutant 5 only at the final overlap of two starts after the winner is done (the post-release check, whose pre-release checks all hold). Existing assertions (whipStarting false and whipTransport null after failure, the 429 check, config restored in finally) stay in the untouched originals; the new tests restore config in finally too. npm run lint and typecheck pass; npm test passes 1303 of 1303.
